title: How Many, but How Sure? Class Competition as a Confidence Proxy in Multi-Class Density-Based Counting
abstract: arXiv:2610.23611v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-class density estimators can count objects in crowded scenes, but their class-wise outputs offer no indication of how reliably density mass has been allocated. We introduce a training-free confidence proxy based on local competition between the strongest class channels. The resulting prominence measure requires only the predicted density maps, with no retraining or access to model internals. We test whether residual competition is diagnostic of cross-class leakage by attenuating contested density at inference time. On DSACA predictions for the Hicks et al. dataset, this reduces overall MAE from 0.920 to 0.846, suggesting that class competition contains useful information about count reliability.

translated_title: 多少个，但有多确定？类别竞争作为多类别基于密度的计数中的置信度代理
translated_abstract: 多类别密度估计器可以在拥挤场景中对物体进行计数，但其按类别划分的输出无法指示密度质量分配的可靠程度。我们引入了一种无需训练的置信度代理，它基于最强的类别通道之间的局部竞争。由此得到的显著性度量只需要预测的密度图，无需重新训练或访问模型内部结构。我们通过在推理时衰减存在竞争的密度，来检验残余竞争是否能够诊断跨类别泄漏。在 Hicks 等人数据集的 DSACA 预测上，该方法将总体 MAE 从 0.920 降低至 0.846，表明类别竞争包含了关于计数可靠性的有用信息。
tldr: 提出一种无需训练的置信度代理方法，利用多类别密度计数中最强类别通道间的局部竞争来衡量计数可靠性，推理时衰减竞争密度可将 Hicks 数据集上的总体 MAE 从 0.920 降至 0.846。
en_tdlr: A training-free confidence proxy based on local competition between the strongest class channels in multi-class density-based counting; attenuating contested density at inference time reduces overall MAE from 0.920 to 0.846 on the Hicks et al. dataset, showing that class competition carries useful information about count reliability.
